title: The specified quotient-completion unit on complete objects
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime, let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite, and let $X$ be any scheme. Let $R=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}$ and $D(R)$ be the completed coefficient sheaf and its unbounded module derived category of [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. Let $C\in D(R)$ satisfy the global derived-completeness predicate [def-weil-derived-complete]. The particular normalized unit $\eta_C:C\to\Lambda C$ of [def-pur-integral-derived-operations] is an isomorphism. Here the normalization is $\eta_{Q(P)}\,;\,\kappa_P=Q(u_P)$ for each flat-term K-flat representative $P$, where $u_P=(c_P,0)$ is the canonical map into the actual shifted cone of $1-s$ on the specified positive-exponent quotient tower. The assertion concerns this unit, rather than the existence of some isomorphism with a derived limit.

source.place: Proposition 3.5.1 and Definition 3.5.2; parent proof Step 4

proof.text: Use the identity extension in [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison]. Compare its ordinary reductions with those of [def-pur-integral-derived-operations] by the scalar-extension universal property: each comparison sends a tensor x to the same a tensor x. These comparisons commute with transitions and the unit. Products and mapping cocones give an isomorphism of augmented Roos complexes. The identity multiplication and the normalized identity equation of the finite-free theorem identify its comparison with the particular (c,0) roosUnit. Thus Q(roosUnit) is invertible on a good representative of C. The defining normalization of completionUnit and its naturality transport this to C.
